claims.text: this module reads, so a fake is three fields, not a mock framework.
claims.why: Comment refers to module-level design decision; no code in chunk confirms or denies.

claims.text: runner(argv, stdin_text) -> RunResult. stdin_text is None when the call sends nothing on stdin (every read path); it carries the comment body on publish.
claims.why: Runner type alias defines stdin_text as str | None, matching the claim.

claims.text: Default runner: actually invoke ``gh``. Never raises -- a launch failure becomes a RunResult the classifier can map to a status.
claims.why: Function catches FileNotFoundError, OSError, TimeoutExpired and returns RunResult; never raises.

claims.text: gh installs as a .CMD shim under some Windows package managers; subprocess cannot spawn it by bare name (WinError 2), so resolve the real path first -- the same lesson codex_cli.py records for the codex shim.
claims.why: Code uses shutil.which(argv[0]) to resolve the path before spawning.

claims.text: gh emits UTF-8 (smart quotes in PR titles, box drawing); without an explicit encoding text=True decodes with the Windows locale and a stray byte kills the capture thread.
Always pass input (possibly ''): it closes the child's stdin, so gh cannot block waiting on an inherited handle that never reaches EOF.
claims.why: input=stdin_text if stdin_text is not None else '' ensures a string is always passed.

claims.text: ``markdown`` is populated on ``dry_run`` and ``published``; it is EMPTY on ``refused_secret`` -- handing the caller a body the floor just rejected invites it straight back into a log file.
claims.why: No code in chunk sets markdown field; claim about behaviour outside this chunk.

claims.text: First present, non-None value among ``names``, read as a mapping key or an attribute. Deliberately alias-tolerant: this renderer must keep working while the council's own dataclasses are still being named.
claims.why: Function iterates names, checks Mapping getattr, returns first non-None.

claims.text: dict-keyed collections (e.g. {vendor: stats}) are flattened into rows carrying their key, so a mapping and a list of rows render identically.
claims.why: Code iterates items, adds 'vendor' key from dict key.

observations.what: shutil.which may return None; code uses it directly as exe leading to potential TypeError.
Encoding forced to utf-8; may mismatch if gh outputs other encoding despite errors='replace'.
_field function returns default if all names are None or absent; but if attribute exists with value None it returns default.
_as_list handles Mapping by iterating items; if Mapping has non-string keys, 'vendor' key may be unexpected type.
